item.title: Indiana bill tightens school gun penalties, eases adult court rule
item.description: A revised Indiana bill targeting youth gun violence is moving forward after lawmakers softened language that would have automatically sent some teens to adult court, while increasing penalties for firearms near schools.

item.title: Indiana Senate sends ‘Let Kids Be Kids’ child supervision bill to governor
item.description: Parents who allow kids to bike, walk or play outside without constant supervision would be shielded from child neglect allegations under a bill sent to Gov. Mike Braun’s desk on Tuesday.

item.title: State announces workshops around the state for feedback on water plan
item.description: The Indiana Department of Natural Resources will host seven workshops across Indiana to allow Hoosiers to provide input on the development of a statewide water inventory and management plan under an executive order by Gov. Mike Braun.

item.title: Amended Indiana syringe services bill would require ID, one-to-one exchange
item.description: An Indiana House committee advanced an amended bill this week that would extend syringe services programs by two years. Some advocates say requirements in the amendment would weaken programs.

item.title: Purdue Polytechnic High School to close South Bend school amid declining enrollment
item.description: The Purdue Polytechnic High School board of directors will close the charter network’s South Bend location amid financial challenges while it focuses on the long-term stability of its two remaining Indianapolis campuses.

item.title: 'We will be forced to close our doors.' Bill regulating hemp products receives industry pushback
item.description: Indiana lawmakers want to close a loophole allowing the sale of hemp products with high THC levels. Many industry workers say it could force them to close.

item.title: Details on long-expected Meta data center campus unveiled
item.description: The worst kept secret in Indiana — Meta building a $10 billion data center campus in Lebanon — was officially unveiled Wednesday with complete details on water, electricity and community investments.

item.title: Utilities answer questions about LEAP district, Eagle Creek water deal
item.description: Deal would send up to 25M gallons of water daily to Boone County, some from Eagle Creek.

item.title: Could Indiana soon approve a 'conservative' SAT for colleges and universities?
item.description: Indiana lawmakers debated a bill that would require public colleges to accept the Classic Learning Test alongside the SAT and ACT. Supporters call it a “back to basics” option, while testing officials question its validation and security.

item.title: Indy charter advocates' use of race 'reeks of paternalism,' coalition spokesman says
item.description: The coalition statement reflects months of tension between lawmakers, reform groups, and community members.
